The Government has also considered the large-scale real-world operating experience. India witnesses approximately 8 crore vehicles visiting retail outlets every day (around 80% petrol vehicles),

The Government's assessment is also based on manufacturer service data. A leading OEM serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025-26, including approximately 1.5 crore vehicles that were not originally certified as E20-compatible, and reported no E20-linked corrosion, abnormal wear or reduction in component life. A leading 2 wheeler company has reported similar field experience.

Further, the rollout of higher ethanol blends was undertaken only after extensive consultation with automobile manufacturers, SIAM, ARAI, component manufacturers, testing agencies and Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).

Material compatibility, engine calibration, drivability, durability, emissions, fuel systems and performance were scientifically evaluated before implementation. Manufacturers have continued to honour vehicle warranties, reflecting their confidence in the compatibility of the fuel.

One OEM recently stated that data from 1.4 crore E20-operated vehicles tracked over an extended period showed no evidence of ethanol-induced corrosion, while ARAI reaffirmed that E20-compatible vehicles undergo rigorous international-standard validation before reaching consumers.

In addition, Oil Marketing Companies maintain strict fuel quality assurance through over 30,000 retail outlet inspections for adulteration and fuel quality verification, supported by directions to States to maintain zero tolerance towards fuel adulteration. Ethanol-blended petrol conforms to BIS specifications and undergoes quality checks throughout the supply chain.

Accordingly, the Government's statement that "no widespread issues" have been reported is based not on isolated instances but on the cumulative evidence of over 25 years of phased implementation, extensive scientific validation, continuous field experience across crores of vehicles, manufacturer service records, stakeholder consultations, and ongoing quality monitoring.

The Government examines claims circulated on social media in consultation with manufacturers and technical agencies. Many such claims have been found to be exaggerated, misleading or unsupported by technical evidence and no verified evidence of widespread engine damage due to ethanol blending has emerged.

Claim 2: Nearly 30 crore vehicles will become unusable.

E15+ blended petrol has already been in widespread use for more than three and a half years, while E19-E20 fuel has been in use for over two and a half years.

During this period:

More than 20 crore two-wheelers

More than 3 crore petrol cars have operated on these fuels without any verified evidence of widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol blending.

If E20 really rendered vehicles unusable, India would have witnessed millions of breakdowns, warranty claims and service campaigns. Nothing of that sort has occurred.

Claim 3: Automobile manufacturers have privately indicated that E20 is not desirable.

On 4 July 2026, the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, along with the Ministry of Heavy Industries and the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, convened a joint press conference where senior executives from Toyota Kirloskar, Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, Hyundai Motor India, TVS Motor Company and Bajaj Auto collectively addressed concerns regarding E20. Their position was unequivocal:

Toyota Kirloskar stated that E20 was introduced only after rigorous testing on older vehicles, describing ethanol as a clean, high-performance fuel that has been used globally for decades. It further emphasised that testing protocols are internationally standardised under UNECE norms and cannot be compromised.

Maruti Suzuki gave what it described as a "statement of confidence" to consumers. Based on 2.84 crore vehicles serviced in FY 2025-26, including more than 1.5 crore older vehicles that were not originally E20-certified, the company reported no E20-related corrosion, abnormal wear, or reduction in component life. It also clarified that the mileage impact is generally limited to 3–3.5%, and that everyday factors such as tyre pressure, driving style, maintenance and traffic have a much larger influence on fuel economy.

Hero MotoCorp, one of the world's largest two-wheeler manufacturers, stated that analysis of its extensive service data found no higher incidence of damage in vehicles operating on E20 compared to earlier fuels.

Hyundai, TVS Motor Company and Bajaj Auto also participated in the same press conference and collectively reaffirmed the industry's confidence in the E20 programme. The panel concluded by reiterating its commitment to the programme and to addressing consumer concerns transparently.

Claim 4: Older vehicles are at risk.

A leading automobile manufacturer serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY 2025-26.

Among them were approximately 1.5 crore vehicles that were never originally certified as E20-compatible.

no abnormal corrosion,

no abnormal wear,

no reduction in component life was attributed to E20 fuel.

A leading two-wheeler manufacturer has reported similar field experience, while another OEM tracked 1.4 crore E20-operated vehicles over an extended period and found no evidence of ethanol-induced corrosion.

Claim 5: Mileage will collapse.

Government studies and automobile manufacturers have consistently explained that fuel efficiency depends on multiple factors, including:

traffic conditions,

vehicle maintenance,

air-conditioner usage.

For certain older E10-designed vehicles, any reduction in fuel economy is generally limited to about 3-5%, not the exaggerated figures being circulated.

At the same time, E20 provides:

higher octane rating, superior anti-knock characteristics,

cleaner combustion, smoother engine performance,

better acceleration and ride quality.

Claim 6: Manufacturers are being forced to support E20.

Had automobile manufacturers not been satisfied with the scientific validation, they would neither

have certified E20-compatible vehicles,

nor continued to honour warranty obligations.

Manufacturers continue to honour warranties for vehicles operating on specification-compliant E20 fuel because they have confidence in the extensive testing that preceded the rollout.

Claim 7: Automobile companies are under Government pressure to hide the truth about E20.

India's automobile manufacturers are independent listed companies with legal and regulatory obligations to their customers.

They cannot conceal widespread vehicle defects without exposing themselves to warranty claims, product liability, regulatory action and serious reputational damage.

Manufacturers continue to honour warranties for E20-compatible vehicles, something they would not do if they believed E20 was causing systemic engine damage. Warranty decisions are based on engineering validation and field experience and not political considerations.

The industry's position has also been expressed publicly and transparently. On 4 July 2026, senior executives from Toyota Kirloskar, Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, Hyundai Motor India, TVS Motor Company and Bajaj Auto jointly addressed the media. headline: Over 25.85 Lakh Scheduled Caste Students in Tamil Nadu Benefitted from Central Scholarship Schemes in Three Years
fullText:

Over 25.85 Lakh Scheduled Caste Students in Tamil Nadu Benefitted from Central Scholarship Schemes in Three Years

Government Strengthens Educational Access, Social Protection and Economic Empowerment Through Scholarships, PM-AJAY, PM-YASASVI and Other Welfare Initiatives

30 JUL 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has reiterated its commitment to advancing educational opportunities, strengthening social protection and promoting economic empowerment for vulnerable communities in Tamil Nadu through a wide range of welfare programmes being implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The initiatives cover Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Economically Backward Classes, Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes, senior citizens, sanitation workers, transgender persons, persons affected by substance abuse and other marginalized groups, with a focus on inclusive development, skill enhancement and improved access to financial assistance.

This information was given by the Hon'ble Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply to Dr. M. Dhanapal in Rajya Sabha.

The Government's flagship scholarship programmes have continued to provide substantial educational support to Scheduled Caste students in Tamil Nadu. Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Castes and Others, the number of beneficiaries increased from 3,35,642 during 2023-24 to 5,21,123 in 2024-25, before rising further to 5,82,684 in 2025-26. Correspondingly, the Central assistance increased from ₹70.56 crores to ₹109.45 crores and further to ₹121.49 crores over the same period.

Similarly, under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste Students, the Government supported 9,34,793 students with Central assistance amounting to ₹1,032.09 crores during 2023-24. In 2024-25, scholarships were provided to 6,43,761 students with financial assistance of ₹713.69 crores. The number of beneficiaries increased substantially in 2025-26, with 9,66,840 Scheduled Caste students receiving scholarships supported by ₹1,034.94 crores. Collectively, the two scholarship schemes benefited more than 25.85 lakh Scheduled Caste students in Tamil Nadu over the last three financial years, while Central assistance exceeded ₹3,080 crores, reaffirming the Government's continued emphasis on ensuring equitable access to quality education for Scheduled Caste students.

The Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyudaya Yojana (PM-AJAY) has also played an important role in improving socio-economic infrastructure and livelihood opportunities for Scheduled Caste communities across Tamil Nadu. Under the Adarsh Gram component of the scheme, the State received ₹18,606.69 lakh during 2023-24, followed by ₹22,325.63 lakh during 2024-25, while ₹165.55 lakhs have been released so far during 2025-26. The financial support under the Grants-in-Aid component also witnessed sustained assistance, with releases amounting to ₹9,182.94 lakh in 2023-24, ₹9,674.36 lakh in 2024-25, and ₹11,962.81 lakh in 2025-26. Assistance was also extended for hostel infrastructure under the scheme to facilitate better educational opportunities for Scheduled Caste students.

The Government has also continued to prioritize the welfare of senior citizens in Tamil Nadu through dedicated financial assistance under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC) and the State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC). Under IPSrC, Central assistance of ₹15.63 crore was released during 2023-24, followed by ₹16.36 crore in 2024-25 and ₹15.78 crore in 2025-26, reflecting the Government's sustained commitment towards strengthening institutional care, health support and welfare services for senior citizens. Under SAPSrC, financial assistance amounted to ₹0.15 crore in 2023-24, while ₹1.43 crore was released during 2025-26 to support State-level initiatives aimed at improving the quality of life of elderly citizens.

The Prime Minister Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India (PM-YASASVI) has continued to expand educational opportunities for students belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Backward Classes (EBCs) and Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs). Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship component, the Government released ₹40.47 crore during 2023-24, ₹23.63 crore during 2024-25, and ₹35.29 crore during 2025-26. The financial assistance under the Post-Matric Scholarship component stood at ₹135 crore in 2023-24, ₹119.37 crore in 2024-25, and ₹106.74 crore in 2025-26. The scheme also supported the construction of hostels for OBC boys and girls, with ₹5.25 crore, ₹1.30 crore, and ₹0.03 crore released over the last three financial years respectively.

The Government has also significantly strengthened support for meritorious students through the Top Class Education components of PM-YASASVI. The financial assistance for Top Class Education in Schools increased from ₹1.88 crore in 2023-24 to ₹11.51 crore in 2024-25, before rising substantially to ₹30.62 crore during 2025-26. Similarly, the assistance under the Top Class Education in Colleges component rose from ₹5.71 crore in 2023-24 to ₹14.79 crore in 2024-25, reaching ₹15.41 crore in 2025-26, reflecting the Government's continued efforts to promote access to quality education among socially and educationally disadvantaged communities.

The National Action for Mechanized Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE), launched in 2023 to ensure the safety and dignity of sewer and septic tank workers, has also made notable progress in Tamil Nadu. According to the information placed before the Rajya Sabha, 6,891 sewer and septic tank workers have been validated in the State, with an equal number of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits distributed. The Government has also provided 37 safety devices to Emergency Response Sanitation Units (ERSUs), organised 98 workshops on the prevention of hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks, and extended capital subsidy for mechanised cleaning equipment to 44 sanitation workers. In addition, 34,854 waste pickers have been validated, while 9,925 PPE kits have been distributed among them to improve occupational safety and dignity.

The Central Government reiterated that the Government remains committed to ensuring that the benefits of education, skill development, social protection, rehabilitation and economic empowerment reach every eligible beneficiary across Tamil Nadu. Through sustained investments in scholarships, livelihood promotion, welfare programmes and inclusive development initiatives, the Ministry continues to work towards building an equitable society where vulnerable communities are empowered to participate fully in the nation's social and economic progress.

headline: Cases Registered Under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Rise to 53,372 in 2023, Convictions and Persons Convicted More Than Double by 2024
fullText:

Cases Registered Under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Rise to 53,372 in 2023, Convictions and Persons Convicted More Than Double by 2024

NCRB Data Shows Cases Registered Against Scheduled Castes Rose from 45,995 in 2020 to a Five-Year High of 53,372 in 2023 in 28 States, Persons Convicted Rise from 4,855 to 7,884 in States & UTs

30 JUL 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment today placed before the Rajya Sabha the detailed State/UT-wise statistics on crimes against members of the Scheduled Castes registered under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, covering the five-year period from 2020 to 2024. The figures are compiled and published by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) in its publication “Crime in India,” the country's official crime-statistics database, whose reports are available up to the year 2024.

This information was given by Hon’ble Minister of State for Social Justice & Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply to the Member of Parliament Shri Sanjay Singh in the Rajya Sabha.

The written reply stated that cases registered under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 stood at 45,995 in 2020, of which 36,178 were chargesheeted, 17,113 remained under investigation at the year-end, and 2,613 ended in conviction. Similarly, a total of 61,925 persons were arrested that year, 75,238 were chargesheeted, and 4,855 were convicted, while 177,379 cases remained pending trial at year-end.

In 2021, cases registered held roughly steady at around 45,800 to 46,100, with 37,123 chargesheeted and about 16,300 to 16,400 pending investigation. The convictions rose to 2,848, arrests totalled roughly 58,700 to 58,800, and around 74,000 to 74,100 persons were chargesheeted. The pending trials climbed further to roughly 2,05,800 to 2,06,000, and 5,141 persons were convicted.

The registrations then rose sharply in 2022 to 52,866 cases, with roughly 42,000 to 42,900 chargesheeted and about 17,000 to 17,200 cases pending investigation. The convictions nearly doubled from the previous year to 4,876. The arrests numbered roughly 65,000 to 65,150, persons chargesheeted numbered between 84,074 and 84,145, and persons convicted rose sharply to roughly 9,070 to 9,080. The cases pending trial rose to between 233,500 and 233,750.

In 2023, cases registered rose again to a five-year high of 53,372, with 45,439 chargesheeted and 14,634 pending investigation. The convictions stood at 4,691. The arrests totalled 61,747, persons chargesheeted numbered 90,664 — the highest of the period — and 7,858 persons were convicted. The pending trials climbed to 2, 62,554.

By 2024, cases registered eased to 48,669, with 40,614 chargesheeted and 14,918 pending investigation. The convictions rose to 5,192, the highest figure in the five-year period, and persons convicted reached 10,839, also a five-year high — more than double the 2020 figure. The arrests totalled 55,286 and persons chargesheeted numbered 84,215, while pending trials rose further to 2, 87,694, also the highest of the period.

The Ministry reiterated that the NCRB’s Crime in India report remains the authoritative, publicly available source for tracking crimes against Scheduled Castes, and that the Government continues to monitor category-wise incidents and case outcomes to inform policy on the safety and security of Scheduled Castes communities, the Minister stated.

headline: IMPLEMENTATION OF RERA ACT, 2016
fullText:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs

IMPLEMENTATION OF RERA ACT, 2016

30 JUL 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi

As per Entry 18 of List- II (State List) of 7th Schedule of Constitution of India, ‘Land’ and ‘Colonization’ are State subjects. However, by deriving powers from Entries 6, 7 & 46 of List-III (Concurrent List) of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 [RERA] was enacted by the Parliament to regulate the contractual relationship between homebuyers and promoters.

RERA aims to ensure transparency & accountability in the Real Estate Sector, thereby protecting the interests of the homebuyers.

RERA mandates the registration of real estate projects with the Regulatory Authority before any advertisement, marketing, booking, or sale and in case of contravention of this provision, the promoter is liable to a penalty of up to 10% of the estimated cost of the real estate project, as determined by the Regulatory Authority. Moreover, a Committee was constituted by this Ministry to address challenges during registration of projects across States / Union Territories (UTs) and recommend steps to ensure registration of eligible projects towards effective implementation of RERA. The report of the Committee has been shared with all the Real Estate Regulatory Authorities for further necessary action.

RERA also mandates the promoters to disclose all necessary project details & approvals and deposit 70% of the amounts realized from homebuyers in a separate bank account, which shall be utilized only for land cost and project construction.

RERA also provides for a fast-track dispute resolution mechanism by making the provision of disposal of matter within 60 days. Section 40 of RERA provides for recovery of unpaid interest, penalty or compensation from the promoter as arrears of land revenue and empowers the Adjudicating Officer, Regulatory Authority or Appellate Tribunal to issue necessary orders or directions.

Further, as per Section 41 of RERA, Central Advisory Council (CAC) has been constituted under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs to advise and recommend the Central Government on all matters concerning the implementation of the Act, including safeguarding the interests of the homebuyers.

Moreover, the Ministry regularly communicates with State Governments on various RERA-related issues, including enhancing the functional and administrative autonomy of Regulatory Authorities and ensuring adequate staff deployment as per operational requirements.

In last one year, the Ministry has held regular consultations with stakeholders including representatives of Homebuyers’ Associations & Real Estate Developers, State Real Estate Regulatory Authorities, among others, for effective implementation of RERA, development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and amendments needed in the Act.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

The Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs highlighted the provisions and enforcement mechanisms of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, focusing on project registration, consumer safeguards, penalties, and stakeholder engagement.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- Entry 18 of List‑II designates land and colonization as State subjects, but RERA was enacted under concurrent list entries 6, 7 & 46.  
- Projects must be registered with the Regulatory Authority before any advertisement, marketing, booking, or sale.  
- Promoters may be penalized up to 10 % of the estimated project cost for contravention.

- Dispute resolution must be completed within 60 days via a fast‑track mechanism.

headline: NATIONAL SMART PUBLIC TRANSPORT MISSION
fullText:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs

NATIONAL SMART PUBLIC TRANSPORT MISSION

30 JUL 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi

‘Urban planning’ is a State subject, therefore, the respective State Governments are responsible for planning, initiating and developing proposal for development of urban infrastructure including public transport project, measures to reduce congestion, improve urban mobility through digital technologies etc. in different cities.

Central Government has issued various policy guidelines like National Urban Transport Policy 2006 and The Metro Policy 2017 for systematic planning and execution of Public Transport project including metro project, which are applicable to all regions of India.

As on date, per se there is no National Smart Public Transport Scheme for integrated public transport, digital ticketing, non- motorized transport, last-mile connectivity.

However, Central Government considers Central Financial Assistance, for deployment of e- buses under various Central Schemes (PM e- Bus Sewa, PM e- Drive etc.) and for implementation of Metro projects as and when posed by concerned State Government. Under above interventions digital ticketing, integrated public Transport etc. are priority items.

National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) is an interoperable card with vision of “One Nation, One Card”, which works seamlessly among different Metro/RRTS and Bus operators. The Ministry has issued directions for implementation of National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) ecosystem based on qSPARC (quick Specification for Payment Application of RuPay Chip) developed by National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It is functional in 13 Metro projects and 11 Bus Transport corporations by ensuring ease of ticketing through these digital technologies, which facilitates shift from private vehicle to public transport thereby reducing traffic congestion.

Further, PM-eBus Sewa Guidelines issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs includes implementation of NCMC based Automatic Fare Collection System (AFCS) for bus operations.

Further, under “Transport Planning and Capacity Building in Urban Transport for metro and non metro projects” sub scheme of MoHUA, various studies like preparation of Integrated Mobility Plan, Detailed Project Reports, Multi Modal integration plans etc. have been eligible components for Central Finance Assistance for cities, ULBs etc. which is considered based on feasibility of proposal as and when posed by concerned State Government.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

Project to Add 6 New Platforms and 6 Additional Lines While Widening of Existing Six Platforms to Handle Growing Passenger Traffic

New East-Side Station Entrance, Electronic Interlocking, Surface Parking and Efficient Circulation Plan to Transform Passenger Experience

30 JUL 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

In a major boost to passenger infrastructure and operational efficiency, Indian Railways has approved the remodelling of the Visakhapatnam Coaching Yard of South Coast Railway at a cost of ₹299 crore. The project aims to significantly enhance the station's handling capacity, improve punctuality and provide modern passenger amenities at one of the busiest railway terminals in the country.

Comprehensive Remodelling of Visakhapatnam Coaching Yard

The sanctioned project includes comprehensive remodelling of the Visakhapatnam Coaching Yard through construction of additional lines and platforms along with Electronic Interlocking (EI).

Visakhapatnam Railway Station is a major coaching terminal handling nearly 80,000 passengers every day with an average of 113 trains daily. Owing to the existing yard layout, terminating and through trains are required to negotiate surface crossings, leading to detention at approach signals, reduced platform availability and operational constraints.

The yard remodelling will minimise the impact of these surface crossings, reduce detention time, improve platform occupancy and enable handling of additional trains.

Major Capacity Enhancement and Passenger-Centric Infrastructure

The scope of work includes:

Dismantling of line loop lines and reorganising the point zones.

Widening of the existing six platforms.

Construction of six additional platforms equipped with modern passenger amenities.

Construction of six additional railway lines.

Development of passenger utilities, including ramps, lifts and escalators on the widened platforms to improve accessibility and passenger convenience.

Creation of a new entrance on the eastern side of the station along with relocation of the Passenger Reservation System (PRS).

Installation of Electronic Interlocking (EI) in the Visakhapatnam station yard along with development of surface parking facilities and an efficient circulating area plan.

Improved Operational Efficiency and Passenger Convenience

The remodelling project will significantly improve operational efficiency by reducing congestion within the coaching yard, increasing platform availability and facilitating smoother movement of trains. The additional infrastructure will enable Visakhapatnam station to handle growing passenger demand while improving punctuality and reducing detention of trains.

headline: DFS Launches Protection & Indemnity Insurance Product under Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP)
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

DFS Launches Protection & Indemnity Insurance Product under Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP)

With the introduction of BMIP, War risk premium rates decrease approximately by 35-40%, from the levels observed at the height of West Asia conflict

A total of 1608 Policies covering Cargo and Hull War risks issued under the Pool as on 29th July 2026

30 JUL 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance held an event chaired by Secretary, DFS today in New Delhi to launch India’s first sovereign-backed Protection & Indemnity insurance product under Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP), designed by the New India Assurance Company Limited.

The event was attended by Director General of Shipping Shri Shyam Jagannathan, senior officers from Department of Financial Services including Additional Secretary Shri Debasish Prusty, and CMD, General Insurance Corporation of India Shri Hitesh Joshi, CMD, New India Assurance Company Limited, Smt. Girija Subramanian, CMD Shipping Corporation of India Limited Capt. Binesh Kumar Tyagi, Secretary General, General Insurance Council Smt. Kasturi Sengupta, senior officers from ICCSA and INSA and Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Shri Sh. Venkatesapathy S.

Speaking on the occasion, Secretary, DFS congratulated all stakeholders involved in the process of formulation of the Protection & Indemnity (P&I) insurance product for achieving this landmark milestone for India’s maritime sector. The Secretary, DFS handed over the first P&I policy document to Shipping Corporation of India Limited issued by the New India Assurance Company Limited under BMIP, providing financial protection against third party liabilities including Crew & Cargo liability, pollution liability, wreck removal, 24x7 port correspondent network with indemnity limit upto USD 1.5 billion, through the combined capacity of the pool.

Since the operationalisation of BMIP by DFS on 12th May, 2026 backed by sovereign guarantee, the pool has demonstrated substantial market acceptance and has successfully met its primary objective of providing uninterrupted war risk insurance capacity to Indian stakeholders. With the introduction of BMIP, the war risk premium rates have decreased approximately by 35-40%, if compared with the levels observed at the height of the West Asia conflict. As on 29th July 2026, a total of 1608 policies covering Cargo War risks and Hull War risks have been issued under the Pool.

While the BMIP mechanism ensures the continuity of maritime war risk insurance coverage, fosters the development of domestic underwriting capacity, and enhances confidence among India's shipping and trade stakeholders, extending the pool to include Protection & Indemnity (P&I) coverage would further strengthen India's maritime risk management framework and improve the resilience of its maritime insurance ecosystem.

This initiative is another step towards the country’s commitment to building resilient, domestic insurance capabilities and supports the broader national vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat by fostering self-reliance in specialized insurance solutions, reducing dependence on foreign markets, and ensuring that value generated from India's maritime trade remains within the domestic economy.

headline: National Advisory Board on Management of Genetic Resources Charts Roadmap for Strengthening India's Agrobiodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Utilization
fullText:

National Advisory Board on Management of Genetic Resources Charts Roadmap for Strengthening India's Agrobiodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Utilization

Board calls for integrated management of plant, animal, fish, microbial and insect genetic resources to support Viksit Bharat and climate-resilient agriculture

30 JUL 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi

Recognising the strategic importance of genetic resources for ensuring India's food, nutrition, environmental and livelihood security, the newly reconstituted ‘National Advisory Board on Management of Genetic Resources (NABMGR)’ held its first meeting on July 29, 2026 at the ICAR–National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (ICAR-NBPGR), New Delhi.

The NABMGR was first constituted by the President of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) in 2011, under the chairmanship of Padma Bhushan Dr R.S. Paroda, Former Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), and Director General, ICAR. In 2026, ICAR reconstituted the Board again under the chairmanship of Dr Paroda and the co-chairmanship of Dr M.L. Jat, Secretary, DARE, and Director General, ICAR. The reconstituted Board brings together experts and key stakeholders to recommend national policies and strategies on agrobiodiversity, to promote coordinated management of plant, animal, fish, microbial, and insect genetic resources and advise on emerging national and international issues related to genetic resources.

The meeting of NABMGR held on July 29, was attended by senior representatives from the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Botanical Survey of India (BSI), National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), National Seed Association of India (NSAI), Bioversity International, Deputy Directors General of ICAR, Directors of the six ICAR National Bureaux managing genetic resources, farmer representatives and other eminent experts.

In his opening remarks, Dr. Paroda observed that India's rich diversity of plant, animal, fish, microbial and insect genetic resources is a national strategic asset that underpins long-term food and nutritional security, climate resilience and sustainable agricultural development. He emphasised the need for strategic prioritisation by each National Bureau so that conservation and management efforts are closely aligned with emerging national needs. He highlighted the importance of enhancing the use of conserved germplasm, including wild relatives/species, in crop, livestock and fish improvement programmes to broaden the genetic base and accelerate the development of climate-resilient and high-performing varieties and breeds.

Dr Paroda recalled the successful organisation of the first International Agrobiodiversity Congress (IAC) in 2016, inaugurated by the Hon'ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi. He urged the effective implementation of the recommendations of the Delhi Declaration on Agrobiodiversity adopted during the Congress. He called for a review of the progress made so far and the preparation of a clear roadmap for future action. Further, he underscored the importance of strengthening international collaboration, particularly with countries in Central Asia and South-East Asia, to facilitate access to valuable genetic resources. He emphasised the need to reinforce existing Memoranda of Understanding and promote strategic exchange of germplasm, especially for crops such as cotton, rambutan, avocado, mangosteen etc. and livestock species such as sheep from these regions. The development of an appropriate legal framework to protect the rights of breeders and farmers for animal and fish genetic resources, on the lines of the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act (PPV&FRA) was also advocated by Dr Paroda. He observed that such a framework would encourage innovation while safeguarding the interests of livestock keepers and fish farmers.

Dr M.L. Jat highlighted that effective management of genetic resources must be closely integrated with advances in soil science, digital agriculture and crop improvement. He stressed that identifying crop accessions best suited to specific soil types and agro-ecological regions would accelerate the development of climate-resilient and location-specific production systems. He noted that India has built a strong and unparalleled National Agricultural Research, Education and Extension System (NAREES), led by ICAR, that significantly facilitated the conservation, characterization and sustainable use of genetic resources, ensuring their availability for both present and future generations. He expressed confidence that the reconstituted NABMGR with representation from relevant Ministries, Departments and ICAR Bureaux, would strengthen inter-agency coordination and provide strategic guidance for the conservation, sustainable use and equitable sharing of benefits arising from India's genetic resources.

During the meeting, the Directors of the six ICAR National Bureaux presented the major achievements of their respective institutes during the period 2021–2026 and outlined their roadmaps for 2026–2031, focusing on initiatives aligned with national priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

The Board deliberated on several strategic issues relating to the conservation and sustainable utilization of agricultural genetic resources. It recommended strengthening pre-breeding programmes to facilitate greater use of conserved germplasm in crop improvement, identifying unexplored regions for systematic germplasm collection during 2026–2031, and enhancing collaboration among the ICAR National Bureaux to develop an integrated national genetic resources management framework. A full-fledged inter-institutional program was recommended for mainstreaming traditional/ opportunity crop varieties/breeds/species of plants, microbes, insects, animals and fishes which was endorsed by the Padma Shri Mr Sunda Ram Verma, a progressive farmer. The Board also reviewed the status of delegation of responsibilities relating to agrobiodiversity from the National Biodiversity Authority to DARE/ICAR under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and discussed measures to strengthen the implementation of Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) provisions. Members deliberated on mainstreaming traditional and underutilised crop varieties, animal breeds, fish species, microorganisms and insects through an inter-institutional programme, and reviewed the progress made in establishing the National Safety Genebank (NSG). Chairman of NBAMGR suggested that efforts be made to complete the NSG in a timely manner so that it can be dedicated to the nation during the centenary celebrations of ICAR (2028-29)

The meeting reaffirmed the Board's commitment to providing strategic policy guidance for conserving and sustainably utilizing India's invaluable genetic resources through greater scientific collaboration, institutional convergence and evidence-based decision-making. The recommendations are expected to strengthen the country's agrobiodiversity governance and contribute significantly to the vision of Viksit Bharat by enhancing agricultural resilience, food security and sustainable development.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Compliance by industries
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Compliance by industries

30 JUL 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

City Specific Clean Air Action Plans have been prepared for 130 cities under National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) mainly to target air pollution sources like soil & road dust, vehicular emissions, waste burning, construction & demolition activities and greening activities.

State Action Plans prepared under NCAP address industrial pollution through framing polices for use of approved fuels by industries, promotion of clean technologies, laydown city gas distribution network to promote use of cleaner fuels, switching conventional fuels to cleaner fuels (gaseous fuels (CNG/ PNG/ CBG) by industries/ commercial units, etc.

Actions towards control of industrial pollution are primarily implemented by industries, while monitoring and enforcement of industrial emission and discharge norms are carried out by the CPCB and State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/Pollution Control Committees (PCCs) through the Consent mechanism under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and necessary action is taken to ensure compliance with the provisions of the said Acts.

As per reports submitted by Urban Local bodies (ULBs), 11,108 industries located in NCAP Cities have transitioned to cleaner fuels such as natural gas, PNG/LNG, LPG, biogas, etc.

Under NCAP, air quality performance linked grant of ₹ 16,423.55 crore has been provided to 130 cities during FY 2019-20 till 2025-26 through XVth Finance Commission (XV FC) Million-Plus Cities Challenge Fund (MPCCF) (in case of 48 Million-Plus cities) and the Central Sector Scheme (CSS) ‘Control of Pollution’ (CP) of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (in case of 82 Non-Attainment cities). So far, cities have reported the utilization of Rs.11,575.54 crore (70.5%) on PRANA portal. District/ City level Implementation and Monitoring Committee under the Chairmanship of District Collector/ Municipal Commissioner periodically monitors the implementation of City clean air action plans under NCAP.

Further, State level Steering Committee under the Chairmanship of Chief Secretary and Air Quality Monitoring Committee under the Chairmanship of Additional Chief Secretary/ Principal Secretary, Environment Department periodically review and monitor the progress of implementation of city action plans and State Action Plans under NCAP.

The focused actions under NCAP have yielded positive results. During 2025-26, 108 cities recorded reductions in annual PM10 concentrations compared to 2017-18, with 72 cities achieving reductions of more than 20% and 26 cities achieving reductions of more than 40%. Further, 14 cities met the National Ambient Air Quality Standards in FY 2025-26, compared to six cities in 2017-18.

Further, during CY 2025, 73 cities recorded reductions in annual PM2.5 concentrations compared to CY 2024, with 17 cities achieving reductions of more than 20%.

This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Environmental clearances in protected areas
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Environmental clearances in protected areas

30 JUL 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has issued Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006 under the powers conferred by sub-section (1) and clause (v) of sub-section (2) of Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. As per the provisions laid down in the EIA Notification, 2006, as amended from time to time, the Projects/ Activities related to Physical Infrastructure including Environmental Services are specified under Item 7 of the Schedule to the EIA Notification, 2006, as amended. Such Projects/Activities are appraised by the Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC) at Central Level for Category ‘A’ projects and State Expert Appraisal Committee (SEAC) at the State/UT Level for Category ‘B’ projects, considering all the environmental implications associated with the project. In some cases, certain stretches of infrastructure projects may fall within or adjoining Tiger Reserves or other Protected Areas. Such proposals, once submitted online through the PARIVESH portal are examined on an ongoing basis by this Ministry. Such proposals (involving Tiger Reserves or other Protected Areas) have to undergo a stringent, multi-tier scrutiny and approval process, i.e. one before the EACs for grant of Environmental Clearance (EC) under the EIA Notification, 2006 and second through competent bodies and authorities for seeking Wildlife Clearance under the relevant provisions of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 read with the Ministry’s guidelines and the directions of the Hon’ble Courts.

For proper scrutiny and appraisal of projects the Ministry has, on the PARIVESH portal, also developed a Decision Support System (DSS), which is a GIS-enabled spatial visualization and analytical platform that integrates multiple geospatial datasets to assess the environmental sensitivity of project locations. It enables automated proximity analysis of projects with respect to Protected Areas, Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZ), forests, wetlands, coastal regulation zones and other environmentally significant features, thereby providing evidence-based inputs to Expert Appraisal Committees (EACs) and regulatory authorities for informed and expeditious decision-making.

Proposals requiring Wildlife Clearance for projects located within Protected Areas or Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs)/Eco-Sensitive Areas (ESAs) or Forest areas, as applicable, are scrutinised through a multi-tiered mechanism involving the State Chief Wild Life Warden, the State Board for Wild Life, and thereafter the cases so recommended, by the Ministry and the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (SCNBWL), which examines the ecological sensitivity of the area, cumulative and specific impacts on wildlife habitats and corridors, and the proposed mitigation measures on a case-to-case basis. The proposals for Wildlife Clearance are recommended by SCNBWL only after due consideration of the impacts, mitigation measures and incorporating appropriate safeguards. Similarly, proposals are granted Environmental Clearance after due consideration of the environmental impacts and incorporation of project-specific environmental safeguards, including mitigation measures prescribed in the Environmental Management Plan (EMP). No construction or other project-related activities can be commenced by the Project Proponents unless prior Wildlife Clearance, as applicable, is obtained under the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

During the financial years 2024–25 and 2025–26, a total of 20 infrastructure projects/activities were granted EC following the aforementioned process where the project site is located, wholly or partly, in a Protected Area or Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ)/Eco-Sensitive Area (ESA), as applicable.

In accordance with the appraisal carried out by the Expert Appraisal Committee at the Centre/ State/ UT level, as applicable, project-specific environmental safeguards as part of the Environmental Clearance conditions to avoid, minimise and mitigate adverse environmental impacts are prescribed. These include measures relating to wildlife protection, habitat conservation, pollution control, compensatory plantation and environmental monitoring, as applicable. The scientific appraisal process and scrutiny at the approval stage ensures that adequate safeguards are incorporated for the protection of ecologically sensitive landscapes.

This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.
